_meta.source: MOE pages on types of schools, schools with specialised curriculum, the Integrated Programme, special educational needs support and the special education journey; SEAB on the SEC and on access arrangements; MOE Education and Career Guidance page
_meta.notes: Read from the primary MOE and SEAB pages, opened in full, on 2026-11-11. Corrected on that reading: NorthLight School and Assumption Pathway School are the specialised schools and award the ITE Skills Certificate, while Crest Secondary School and Spectra Secondary School are secondary schools for Posting Group 1 whose students graduate with the SEC and an ITE Skills Subject Certificate; the school support officer is the Special Educational Needs (SEN) Officer; the old source address returned 404. Every kind still carries status provisional because the schools lint requires it; the rows for government, independent, Integrated Programme, specialised independent, specialised and special education schools were all read on the primary pages. Still not read on a primary page: the SG Enable row beyond the School to Work Transition Programme, and what the specialised independent schools lead to. This page names what exists and deliberately does not advise. This build has no business giving guidance on special educational needs, so each row says what a thing is, who it is for and how to ask for it, and stops there. The appliesHere field says where this app's own planner does not fit.

kinds.label: A government or government aided secondary school
kinds.sits: The Singapore Cambridge Secondary Education Certificate, with subjects at G1, G2 and G3.
kinds.leadsTo: Every destination this app plans for, from ITE to junior college.
kinds.note: This is the road the whole app assumes. Everything in Plan, Play and Act is built for it.

kinds.label: An independent school
kinds.examples: Schools that set their own fees and develop their own programmes.
kinds.sits: The SEC, and some also run an Integrated Programme alongside it.
kinds.leadsTo: The same destinations. The fee is the difference, and the Independent School Bursary exists for it.
kinds.note: The subject planner applies exactly as written. The money page has the fee and the bursary.

kinds.label: An Integrated Programme
kinds.examples: Six years through to the A Levels, the International Baccalaureate Diploma or the NUS High School Diploma. Open to Posting Group 3.
kinds.sits: No SEC in Secondary 4. The final qualification comes at the end of Year 6.
kinds.leadsTo: University. MOE expects students to stay for the full six years.
kinds.note: The subject planner assumes an exam at sixteen, so its arithmetic does not apply. Everything about work, money, wants and the years to twenty does.

kinds.label: A specialised independent school
kinds.examples: NUS High School of Mathematics and Science, School of the Arts, Singapore Sports School, School of Science and Technology.
kinds.sits: Depends on the school. Its own diploma, the International Baccalaureate, or the SEC.
kinds.leadsTo: Universities here and abroad, conservatoires, sport, and every route in this app.
kinds.note: Where the school runs its own diploma there is no SEC to plan, so use the work, money and wants pages. Entry is through DSA, or by direct application to the Sports School.

kinds.label: A specialised school, or Crest or Spectra Secondary
kinds.examples: NorthLight School and Assumption Pathway School are the specialised schools. Crest and Spectra are secondary schools for Posting Group 1.
kinds.sits: NorthLight and Assumption Pathway: the ITE Skills Certificate. Crest and Spectra: the SEC, with an ITE Skills Subject Certificate.
kinds.leadsTo: Work or ITE from the specialised schools. ITE Nitec or Higher Nitec courses from Crest and Spectra.
kinds.note: This app's planner does not model the ITE Skills Certificate. Crest and Spectra students take SEC subjects at G1, some at G2, so the planner fits them in part. The work page and the ITE route apply in full.

kinds.label: A special education school
kinds.examples: Government funded schools run by social service agencies, for students up to eighteen.
kinds.sits: A curriculum set for the student, which may include national exams or may not.
kinds.leadsTo: Open or supported employment, further training including ITE for some students, and day activity centres.
kinds.note: This app does not model this road and should not pretend to. Transition planning inside the school is the real instrument, and SG Enable runs the school to work programmes.

kinds.label: Not in a mainstream school right now
kinds.examples: Private candidates, home education, students returning after time away.
kinds.sits: The SEC as a private candidate, or another qualification.
kinds.leadsTo: The same destinations. Singapore Citizen and Permanent Resident private candidates can use the 2028 admissions exercise.
kinds.note: The admission arithmetic applies as published. Registration as a private candidate goes through SEAB rather than through a school.

support.label: Access arrangements for exams
support.what: Extra time, a reader, a scribe, a separate room, enlarged print and others, for the national exams.
support.who: Students with special educational needs, including specific physical and learning disabilities.
support.howToGet: Applied for through the school, up to one year before the national exam. Late applications are not accepted.
support.note: This is not an advantage and it is not a favour. It removes something that was measuring the wrong thing.

support.label: The Special Educational Needs (SEN) Officer
support.what: A member of staff who gives support in class, and intervention and skills training alone or in small groups.
support.who: Students with special educational needs in a mainstream school.
support.howToGet: Ask the form teacher who the school's SEN Officer is.
support.note: Often the person who knows most about how a particular student learns, and the least asked for by name.

support.label: Transition planning
support.what: An Individual Transition Plan for life after school, drawn up with the student, the family and post school agencies.
support.who: Students in special education schools, during the secondary school years.
support.howToGet: It is part of the school's programme. The family is meant to be in the room for it.
support.note: The real version of what this app does, run by people who know the student.

support.label: SG Enable
support.what: The agency for disability in Singapore. School to work programmes, training, employment support and funding.
support.who: Students and adults with disabilities, and their families.
support.howToGet: Directly, and the school can make the introduction.
support.note: The School to Work Transition Programme starts in the final school year and runs up to a year after graduation.

support.label: The ECG counsellor, for this in particular
support.what: The person in the school whose job is exactly the join between a student's situation and what comes next.
support.who: Every student in a mainstream secondary school has one.
support.howToGet: Ask your school how to book a session. The ECG Centre at MOE also takes appointments, online or by phone.
support.note: Where this app stops, that conversation starts. Nothing on these pages replaces it.
